---

## formal
Let $Q(m) = \sum_{k}m_{k}/(\sum_{k}\sqrt{m_{k}})^{2}$ for positive triples, the quotient of Proposition \claimref{families.linear-conjecture-refuted-data}, and let $t_{*} = 3/\sqrt{2} - 2$, the positive root of $2t^{2} + 8t - 1$, so that $t_{*}^{2} = \tfrac{17}{2} - 6\sqrt{2} \in (0.01471, 0.01472)$. As in Theorem \claimref{synthesis.mass-ordered-dressing-cannot-spoil-koide}, label a sector's measured masses $m = (m_{1}, m_{2}, m_{3})$ in increasing order and call $b$ a bracket of $m$ under the dressing $D$ if $m_{k} = D_{k}b_{k}$ with $D_{k} > 0$; it is a Koide bracket if $Q(b) = \tfrac23$. The mass values are the stored quantities: own scale ($m_{u}$, $m_{d}$, $m_{s}$ at $2$ GeV, $m_{c}(m_{c})$, $m_{b}(m_{b})$, $m_{t}$ direct) and the running masses at $M_{Z}$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Middle-mass bound.)} Every positive triple with $Q = \tfrac23$ has its middle entry at least $t_{*}^{2}$ times its largest entry, with equality exactly when its two smaller entries are equal.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(The up quarks.)} $m_{c}/m_{t} \in (0.00737, 0.00738)$ at own scale and $(0.00360, 0.00361)$ at $M_{Z}$, both below $t_{*}^{2}$, while $m_{s}/m_{b}$ lies above it at both. Hence no triple $(x, m_{c}, m_{t})$ with $0 < x \le m_{c}$ satisfies the Koide relation, whatever $x$; every Koide bracket of the up sector with $D_{c} \ge D_{t}$ has $b_{u} > b_{c}$; and a Koide bracket of the up sector with the bracket order kept, $b_{u} \le b_{c} \le b_{t}$, needs $D_{t}/D_{c} \ge t_{*}^{2}m_{t}/m_{c}$, which lies in $(1.99, 2.00)$ at own scale and $(4.08, 4.09)$ at $M_{Z}$.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(The class $D_{2} > D_{3} > D_{1}$.)} Part (iv) of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.mass-ordered-dressing-cannot-spoil-koide} applies to this class with $R = D_{3}/D_{1}$, so a Koide bracket in it needs $D_{3}/D_{1} \ge R^{*}$. The sharp bound is $D_{3}/D_{1} \ge R_{1}$, $R_{1}$ the least $R$ with $Q(Rm_{1}, m_{2}, m_{3}) \le \tfrac23$: $R_{1} \in (7.88, 7.89)$ (down, own scale), $(11.00, 11.01)$ (down, $M_{Z}$), $(2010.2, 2010.3)$ (up, own scale), $(4799.8, 4799.9)$ (up, $M_{Z}$). In the class $D_{1} > D_{3} > D_{2}$ a Koide bracket needs $D_{3}/D_{2} \ge R_{2}$, $R_{2}$ the least $R$ with $Q(m_{1}, Rm_{2}, m_{3}) \le \tfrac23$: $R_{2} \in (2.19, 2.20)$, $(2.63, 2.64)$, $(9.36, 9.37)$, $(19.33, 19.34)$ in the same order. Both classes contain Koide brackets in both sectors, so these are thresholds and not exclusions; in the up sector a Koide bracket of the class $D_{2} > D_{3} > D_{1}$ has $b_{u}/b_{t} \ge R_{1}m_{u}/m_{t} > b_{c}/b_{t}$, the bracket order reversed, as (ii) requires.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(No ordering of the factors escapes.)} In both quark sectors and at both sets of values, a Koide bracket needs, whatever the order of its dressing factors, $\max_{j \le 2}D_{3}/D_{j} \ge R^{*}$, with $R^{*}$ in the intervals of the stored theorem, $(1.88, 1.89)$, $(2.19, 2.20)$, $(8.67, 8.68)$ and $(17.5, 17.6)$ in the same order as in (iii), the least value being reached only with $D_{1} = D_{2}$; with $D_{2} > D_{3} > D_{1}$ the heaviest is favoured over the lightest by at least $R_{1}$, and in the up sector the bracket order of $u$ and $c$ is then reversed.
\end{enumerate}
So the remaining class of the stored theorem gives no escape: a Koide bracket for either quark sector needs a dressing that favours the heaviest quark, and none of the classes is excluded by the data alone. Whether the quark brackets satisfy the relation is decided only by a dressing law, which no stored premise supplies.

## technical
The stored theorem on mass-ordered dressing leaves open, in its own words, dressings that raise the middle quark mass and lower the lightest relative to the heaviest. Its corner bound in fact covers them: the bound holds whatever the light factors are, as long as neither exceeds the corner value, and in that class only the lightest factor exceeds one. The sharp bound in the class is larger: the lightest quark must be suppressed relative to the heaviest by at least $7.88$ (down quarks at own scale) and about $2010$ (up quarks at own scale), and by more at the $Z$ mass. A short exact lemma adds a parameter-free necessary condition: in any triple satisfying Koide's relation the middle mass is at least $17/2 - 6\sqrt{2}$, about $0.0147$, of the largest, with equality only when the two lighter masses coincide. The charm-to-top ratio is $0.0074$ at own scale and $0.0036$ at the $Z$ mass, both below that bound, so no value of the up-quark mass below the charm mass makes the up triple satisfy the relation, and any Koide bracket in which the charm is dressed up at least as much as the top must put the up bracket above the charm bracket. Keeping the bracket order needs the top favoured over the charm by about $2$ at own scale and $4.1$ at the $Z$ mass. The down quarks pass the lemma ($m_{s}/m_{b}$ about $0.022$). Every class contains Koide brackets, so the data decide nothing by themselves: the question is whether a dressing that favours the heaviest quark by these factors exists, and the store has no dressing law.

## lay
A formula due to Koide fits the electron, muon and tau masses remarkably well but fails for both families of quarks. One idea is that the quarks' underlying masses obey it and the strong force then shifts them. An earlier result showed that the known strong-force effects shift them the wrong way, and that only an effect favouring the heaviest quark could work; it left one kind of shift unexamined. This result examines it and finds no way out: that kind of shift also needs the heaviest quark strongly favoured, by a factor of at least about eight for the down-type quarks and about two thousand for the up-type quarks. It also proves a simple fact about any three numbers satisfying the formula: the middle one is at least about one and a half percent of the largest. The charm quark is well under one percent of the top quark's mass, so the up-type quarks would fail the formula whatever the up quark's mass below the charm mass, and the shift would have to reorder the up and charm quarks underneath. The data alone cannot settle whether quark masses obey the formula underneath; that needs a rule for the shift, which the series does not have.

## one-liner
Every Koide triple has its middle entry at least $\tfrac{17}{2} - 6\sqrt{2} \approx 0.0147$ of its largest, which $m_{c}/m_{t}$ ($0.0074$, $0.0036$ at $M_{Z}$) violates, so no up triple with $x \le m_{c}$ is Koide; the stored corner bound covers the class $D_{2} > D_{3} > D_{1}$, whose sharp threshold is $D_{3}/D_{1} \ge 7.88$ (down) and $2010$ (up, bracket order of $u$ and $c$ reversed): no ordering of the dressing factors escapes a dressing favouring the heaviest quark, and the data alone cannot decide the question.

proofs.proof-main.tex:
Write $s_{k} = \sqrt{b_{k}}$, $S_{1} = \sum_{k}s_{k}$, $S_{2} = \sum_{k}s_{k}^{2}$, so $Q = S_{2}/S_{1}^{2}$ (Proposition \claimref{families.linear-conjecture-refuted-data}). Two facts of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.mass-ordered-dressing-cannot-spoil-koide} are used: (a) $Q$ is homogeneous of degree zero, its part (i); (b) its part (ii): $\partial Q/\partial s_{j} = 2(S_{1}s_{j} - S_{2})/S_{1}^{3}$, which is negative whenever $3s_{j} \le s_{\max}$, so raising a root that stays at most a third of the largest root strictly lowers $Q$.

\emph{(i)} By (a) take the largest root $s_{3} = 1$ and order $s_{1} \le s_{2} \le 1$. A direct computation gives
\[
Q(t, t, 1) - \tfrac23 = \frac{3(2t^{2} + 1) - 2(2t + 1)^{2}}{3(2t + 1)^{2}} = -\frac{2t^{2} + 8t - 1}{3(2t + 1)^{2}},
\]
positive for $0 \le t < t_{*}$ and zero at $t = t_{*}$, where $t_{*} = -2 + \sqrt{72}/4 = 3/\sqrt{2} - 2 \in (0.1213, 0.1214)$, below $\tfrac13$. Suppose $s_{2} < t_{*}$. Raising $s_{1}$ to $s_{2}$ keeps it below $\tfrac13 = s_{3}/3$, so by (b) $Q(s_{1}, s_{2}, 1) \ge Q(s_{2}, s_{2}, 1) > \tfrac23$. So $Q = \tfrac23$ forces $s_{2} \ge t_{*}$, that is $b_{2} \ge t_{*}^{2}b_{3}$ with $t_{*}^{2} = \tfrac92 - 6\sqrt{2} + 4 = \tfrac{17}{2} - 6\sqrt{2}$. If $s_{2} = t_{*}$ and $s_{1} < t_{*}$, the same step is strict, $Q > \tfrac23$; so equality needs $s_{1} = s_{2} = t_{*}$, and $(t_{*}^{2}, t_{*}^{2}, 1)$ has $Q = \tfrac23$. For a rational $r$, $r < t_{*}^{2}$ exactly when $r < \tfrac{17}{2}$ and $(\tfrac{17}{2} - r)^{2} > 72$, decided in rationals. The check confirms the identity on rational samples, the brackets $t_{*} \in (0.1213, 0.1214)$ and $t_{*}^{2} \in (0.01471, 0.01472)$, and $Q > \tfrac23$ on a rational grid of the square $s_{1}, s_{2} \le 0.1213$.

\emph{(ii)} From the stored quantities (GeV): $m_{c}/m_{t} = 1.2730/172.57$ and $0.619/171.7$, in the stated intervals, and the rational test of (i) shows both below $t_{*}^{2}$; $m_{s}/m_{b} = 0.0935/4.18$ and $0.055/2.89$ are above it. For $0 < x \le m_{c}$ the triple $(x, m_{c}, m_{t})$ has middle entry $m_{c}$ and largest $m_{t}$, so by (i) $Q \ne \tfrac23$ (in fact $Q > \tfrac23$; the check also certifies $Q(m_{c}, m_{c}, m_{t}) > \tfrac23$ with rational bounds on the roots). Let $b$ be a Koide bracket of the up sector with $D_{c} \ge D_{t}$. Then $b_{c}/b_{t} = (m_{c}/m_{t})(D_{t}/D_{c}) \le m_{c}/m_{t} < t_{*}^{2} < 1$. If $b_{u} \le b_{c}$, the triple $b$ has largest entry $b_{t}$ and middle entry $b_{c}$, against (i). So $b_{u} > b_{c}$. If the bracket order is kept, $b_{u} \le b_{c} \le b_{t}$, then (i) gives $b_{c} \ge t_{*}^{2}b_{t}$, that is $D_{t}/D_{c} \ge t_{*}^{2}m_{t}/m_{c}$; by the equality case of (i) this is the value $\rho$ at which $Q(\rho m_{c}, \rho m_{c}, m_{t}) = \tfrac23$, and the check certifies $Q > \tfrac23$ at $\rho = 1.99$, $Q < \tfrac23$ at $\rho = 2.00$ (own scale) and the same at $4.08$ and $4.09$ ($M_{Z}$), with $9\rho m_{c} \le m_{t}$ at the upper ends so that $Q(\rho m_{c}, \rho m_{c}, m_{t})$ is strictly decreasing in $\rho$ there by (b).

\emph{(iii)} By (a) normalise $D_{3} = 1$, so $b = (\rho_{1}m_{1}, \rho_{2}m_{2}, m_{3})$ with $\rho_{j} = D_{3}/D_{j}$; the class $D_{2} > D_{3} > D_{1}$ is $\rho_{2} < 1 < \rho_{1}$. Part (iv) of the stored theorem assumes only $\rho_{j} \in (0, R]$ for $j = 1, 2$ and $Rm_{j} \le m_{3}/9$; with $R = \rho_{1}$ these hold for $\rho_{1} \le R^{*}$, so its bound applies in the class. For the sharp bound, $f_{1}(\rho) = Q(\rho m_{1}, m_{2}, m_{3})$ is continuous and, by (b), strictly decreasing on $1 \le \rho \le m_{3}/(9m_{1})$; the check certifies $f_{1} > \tfrac23$ at the lower and $f_{1} < \tfrac23$ at the upper end of each stated interval, both inside that range, so $R_{1}$ is the unique crossing and lies in the interval. If $\rho_{1} < R_{1}$, then raising $\sqrt{\rho_{2}m_{2}}$ to $\sqrt{m_{2}}$ (allowed by (b), since $9m_{2} \le m_{3}$ and $9\rho_{1}m_{1} < m_{3}$) lowers $Q$, so $Q(b) \ge Q(\rho_{1}m_{1}, m_{2}, m_{3}) = f_{1}(\rho_{1}) > \tfrac23$, the last step by the strict decrease of $f_{1}$ (here $\rho_{1} < R_{1} \le m_{3}/(9m_{1})$); hence $\rho_{1} \ge R_{1}$. The class $D_{1} > D_{3} > D_{2}$, $\rho_{1} < 1 < \rho_{2}$, is the same argument with the roles of $m_{1}$ and $m_{2}$ exchanged and $f_{2}(\rho) = Q(m_{1}, \rho m_{2}, m_{3})$, strictly decreasing on $1 \le \rho \le m_{3}/(9m_{2})$, which contains the stated intervals. That both classes contain Koide brackets: the check certifies $Q < \tfrac23$ at $\rho_{2} = 0.99$ with $\rho_{1} = 9, 13, 2200, 5200$ (and $Q > \tfrac23$ at $\rho_{1} = 1$), so by continuity in $\rho_{1}$ there is a Koide bracket with $\rho_{2} = 0.99$ and $\rho_{1}$ between, in the class $D_{2} > D_{3} > D_{1}$; for $D_{1} > D_{3} > D_{2}$ the check certifies $Q < \tfrac23$ at $\rho_{1} = 0.99$ with $\rho_{2} = 2.4, 2.9, 10, 21$, and $Q > \tfrac23$ at $\rho_{2} = 1$, which gives a Koide bracket in that class in the same way. In the up sector a Koide bracket of the class has $b_{u}/b_{t} = \rho_{1}m_{u}/m_{t} \ge R_{1}m_{u}/m_{t}$, and the check certifies $R_{1}m_{u} > m_{c} > \rho_{2}m_{c}$ at both mass sets, so $b_{u} > b_{c}$, in agreement with (ii).

\emph{(iv)} If $D_{3} \le D_{j}$ for $j = 1, 2$, part (ii) of the stored theorem (with its ninth condition, true for the measured values) gives $Q(b) \ge Q(m) > \tfrac23$, by its part (iii); so $\max_{j}\rho_{j} > 1$, and by its part (iv) with $R = \max_{j}\rho_{j}$, $Q(b) \ge Q(Rm_{1}, Rm_{2}, m_{3})$, which exceeds $\tfrac23$ for $R < R^{*}$. If $\max_{j}\rho_{j} = R^{*}$ and $\rho_{1} \ne \rho_{2}$, one of them is below $R^{*}$ and by (b) the inequality is strict, $Q(b) > \tfrac23$; so the least value is reached only at $\rho_{1} = \rho_{2} = R^{*}$. The two remaining strict orderings are the classes of (iii), with their sharper bounds; the up-sector reversal is (ii). The intervals for $R^{*}$ are those of the stored theorem; the check recertifies their upper ends from the stored quantities ($Q < \tfrac23$ at $\rho_{1} = \rho_{2} = 1.89$, $2.20$, $8.68$, $17.56$) and confirms on a rational grid inside the class $D_{2} > D_{3} > D_{1}$ with $\rho_{1}$ below the lower ends that $Q > \tfrac23$.

check_py:
"""synthesis.koide-middle-mass-bound-closes-the-remaining-quark-dressing-class: exact checks.

Q(m) = sum m_k / (sum sqrt m_k)^2. Square roots of data enter only through certified rational bounds (integer
square roots at scale 10^-12), and every inequality is decided with the bound that makes it harder to pass.
t* = 3/sqrt(2) - 2 is the positive root of 2t^2 + 8t - 1, and t*^2 = 17/2 - 6 sqrt(2); a rational r satisfies
r < t*^2 exactly when r < 17/2 and 72 < (17/2 - r)^2, decided in rationals with no square root.
(1) The middle-mass lemma: Q(t, t, 1) - 2/3 = -(2t^2 + 8t - 1)/(3(2t + 1)^2) as rational functions (sampled), a
    rational bracket of t* and of t*^2, Q > 2/3 on a rational grid of [0, t_lo]^2 with the heaviest root 1, and
    Q(t_hi, t_hi, 1) < 2/3.
(2) The up sector: m_c/m_t < t*^2 at the own-scale and the M_Z values (stored quantities), while m_s/m_b > t*^2 in
    the down sector at both; Q(m_c, m_c, m_t) > 2/3, so (x, m_c, m_t) with x <= m_c is never a Koide triple; an
    order-preserving Koide bracket of the up sector needs D_t/D_c in (1.99, 2.00) or above (own scale), (4.08, 4.09)
    or above (M_Z).
(3) The remaining class D2 > D3 > D1: the least D3/D1 with Q(R m_1, m_2, m_3) <= 2/3 is certified in (7.88, 7.89),
    (11.00, 11.01), (2010.2, 2010.3), (4799.8, 4799.9); the class D1 > D3 > D2 needs D3/D2 in (2.19, 2.20),
    (2.63, 2.64), (9.36, 9.37), (19.33, 19.34) or above; the ninth conditions hold at the upper ends; and each class
    contains Koide brackets (an explicit certified point), so it is a threshold, not an exclusion.
(4) The stored lemma (iv) covers the class: on a rational grid of points with D2 > D3 > D1 and D3/D1 below the stored
    corner value, Q stays above Q(R m_1, R m_2, m_3) > 2/3.
"""
from fractions import Fraction as F

import GA
from tp_premise import premise, quantity

SCALE = 10 ** 12
TWO3 = F(2, 3)
HALF17 = F(17, 2)


def isqrt(n):
    if n < 0:
        raise ValueError
    x = int(n)
    if x == 0:
        return 0
    r = 1 << ((x.bit_length() + 1) // 2)
    while True:
        y = (r + x // r) // 2
        if y >= r:
            return r
        r = y


def sqrt_bounds(q):
    q = F(q)
    n = (q * SCALE * SCALE).__floor__()
    lo = isqrt(n)
    return F(lo, SCALE), F(lo + 1, SCALE)


def Q_s(s):
    S1 = sum(s, F(0))
    return sum((x * x for x in s), F(0)) / (S1 * S1)


def Q_gt(m):
    hi = sum((sqrt_bounds(x)[1] for x in m), F(0))
    return 3 * sum(m, F(0)) > 2 * hi * hi


def Q_lt(m):
    lo = sum((sqrt_bounds(x)[0] for x in m), F(0))
    return 3 * sum(m, F(0)) < 2 * lo * lo


def below_tstar_sq(r):
    """r < 17/2 - 6 sqrt 2, exactly."""
    r = F(r)
    return r < HALF17 and 72 < (HALF17 - r) ** 2


def above_tstar_sq(r):
    r = F(r)
    return r < HALF17 and (HALF17 - r) ** 2 < 72


def gev(qid, scale=F(1)):
    return scale * F(quantity(qid))


def down_own():
    return [gev("quantity.down-quark-mass", F(1, 1000)), gev("quantity.strange-quark-mass", F(1, 1000)),
            gev("quantity.bottom-quark-mass")]


def down_mz():
    return [gev("quantity.down-quark-mass-mz", F(1, 1000)), gev("quantity.strange-quark-mass-mz", F(1, 1000)),
            gev("quantity.bottom-quark-mass-mz")]


def up_own():
    return [gev("quantity.up-quark-mass", F(1, 1000)), gev("quantity.charm-quark-mass"),
            gev("quantity.top-quark-mass")]


def up_mz():
    return [gev("quantity.up-quark-mass-mz", F(1, 1000)), gev("quantity.charm-quark-mass-mz"),
            gev("quantity.top-quark-mass-mz")]


def sets():
    return {"down own": down_own(), "down MZ": down_mz(), "up own": up_own(), "up MZ": up_mz()}


# (1) --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

def check_middle_mass_lemma():
    premise("families.linear-conjecture-refuted-data")
    premise("synthesis.mass-ordered-dressing-cannot-spoil-koide")
    ok = True
    want = {F(0): F(1), F(1, 9): F(83, 121), F(1, 8): F(33, 50), F(3, 10): F(59, 128), F(7, 5): F(123, 361),
            F(2): F(9, 25)}
    for t, q in want.items():
        ok = ok and Q_s([t, t, F(1)]) == q
        ok = ok and q - TWO3 == -(2 * t * t + 8 * t - 1) / (3 * (2 * t + 1) ** 2)
    # sign pattern of Q(t, t, 1) - 2/3 on the samples: above 2/3 below t*, below 2/3 above it
    ok = ok and [q > TWO3 for q in want.values()] == [True, True, False, False, False, False]
    # rational bracket of t*: 2t^2 + 8t - 1 changes sign
    t_lo, t_hi = F(1213, 10000), F(1214, 10000)
    p = lambda t: 2 * t * t + 8 * t - 1
    ok = ok and p(t_lo) < 0 < p(t_hi)
    # and of t*^2 = 17/2 - 6 sqrt 2, decided without roots
    ok = ok and below_tstar_sq(t_lo * t_lo) and above_tstar_sq(t_hi * t_hi)
    ok = ok and below_tstar_sq(F(1471, 100000)) and above_tstar_sq(F(1472, 100000))
    ok = ok and 3 * t_hi < 1 and t_hi - t_lo == F(1, 10000)
    # Q > 2/3 whenever both lighter roots are at most t_lo (heaviest root 1): grid, corner included
    n = 0
    for a in range(0, 13):
        for b in range(a, 13):
            s1, s2 = t_lo * F(a, 12), t_lo * F(b, 12)
            ok = ok and Q_s([s1, s2, F(1)]) > TWO3
            n += 1
    ok = ok and n == 91
    # the bound is attained only at the degenerate triple: just above t*, both equal, Q < 2/3
    ok = ok and Q_s([t_hi, t_hi, F(1)]) < TWO3 and Q_s([t_lo, t_lo, F(1)]) > TWO3

def check_stored_corner_bound_covers_the_class():
    premise("synthesis.mass-ordered-dressing-cannot-spoil-koide")
    s = sets()
    corner_lo = {"down own": F(188, 100), "down MZ": F(219, 100), "up own": F(867, 100), "up MZ": F(1755, 100)}
    corner_hi = {"down own": F(189, 100), "down MZ": F(220, 100), "up own": F(868, 100), "up MZ": F(1756, 100)}
    ok = True
    # the stored corner values R* lie in these intervals for the stored quantities (crossing certified both ways)
    for k, m in s.items():
        R = corner_hi[k]
        ok = ok and Q_lt([R * m[0], R * m[1], m[2]]) and 9 * R * m[1] <= m[2]
    n = 0
    for k, m in s.items():
        R = corner_lo[k]
        ok = ok and Q_gt([R * m[0], R * m[1], m[2]])
        for a in range(1, 5):
            for b in range(1, 5):
                rho1 = 1 + (R - 1) * F(a, 5)          # 1 < rho1 < R
                rho2 = F(b, 5)                        # rho2 < 1
                ok = ok and Q_gt([rho1 * m[0], rho2 * m[1], m[2]])
                n += 1
    ok = ok and n == 64
    GA.check("the stored corner bound applies with R = D3/D1 inside the class D2 > D3 > D1", ok)
    return ok
